section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Briefly review the Power Rule. Introduce the 'Box Model' visualization: If a rectangle's sides are functions f(x) and g(x), how does its total area change when both sides grow?
section_1.example: Visualize a growing digital billboard: as both width and height increase, the new area includes the 'side' growth and the 'corner' overlap.

section_2.title: The Product Rule (0:45-2:00)
section_2.content: Formalize the rule: d/dx [f(x)g(x)] = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x). Use animation to show the two rectangles adding onto the original area to represent the instantaneous change.
section_2.example: A squirrel collecting nuts: f(x) is the number of trees and g(x) is the nuts per tree. The rate of change is the gain from finding new trees plus the gain from finding more nuts in existing trees.

section_3.title: Transitioning to Nested Functions (2:00-2:30)
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Russian Doll' or 'Layered Onion' analogy. Explain that for composite functions f(g(x)), the outer function acts on the output of the inner function.
section_3.example: A robot's arm: The rotation of the shoulder (outer) depends on the battery power (inner) which is also changing.

section_4.title: The Chain Rule (2:30-4:15)
section_4.content: Formalize the rule: d/dx [f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x). Use a 'Gears' animation: Turning the first gear (inner function) at a certain speed causes the second gear (outer function) to turn at a magnified speed based on their sizes.
section_4.example: A rocket launch: The height (f) depends on the fuel (g), and the fuel depends on time (x). The total velocity is the rate of change of height per unit of fuel, multiplied by the rate of fuel consumption.

section_5.title: Synthesis & Summary (4:15-5:00)
section_5.content: Show a 'Hybrid Problem' where both rules are needed. Recap the 'Differentiate the outside, keep the inside, multiply by the derivative of the inside' mnemonic.
section_5.example: Calculate the derivative of y = (x^2 + 1)^3 * sin(x). Identify the Product Rule as the 'skeleton' and the Chain Rule as the 'muscle' for the first term.
